an3.100:1.1: The discourse begins with two quoted propositions. In each, the subject is referred to by the normal word _purisa_ (“person”) and hence might well be a non-Buddhist saying. For the subsequent discussion, the Buddha switches to his preferred technical term _puggala_ (“individual”).
an3.100:1.2: This proposition imagines that the deed is the same as that which is experienced.
an3.100:1.4: Morally potent deeds (_kamma_) have a characteristic or fitting result: good deeds lead to happiness, bad deeds lead to suffering. The result may differ in specifics, but always shares that same character. The notion of a deed that is “to be experienced” (_vedanīya_) in a certain manner or place is explored further in [an9.13](), [an10.219](), and [thag1.81]().
an3.100:1.6: “Lingers” is _khāyati_. Trace to Sanskrit _kṣi_ in the sense, “inhabits, remains”, as Agni “remains” within all creatures (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 14.1.2.24).
an3.100:2.2: _Bhāvitakāya_ is explained in [mn36:9.8]() as ability to endure pain. | Follow Bodhi in emending _appadukkhavihārī_ to _dukkhavihārī_.
an3.100:4.1: At Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.13.1–2, Uddālaka questions Śvetaketu about a lump of salt in a bowl; the taste of salt pervades all just as the self pervades all.
an3.100:10.3: This characterization the justice system, cynical as it is, remains true today.
